title: Suvendu orders district crop-loss reports as Akvan's rain soaks south Bengal
dek: Nadia recorded 91.8 mm and Kolkata more than 50 mm on Friday. Farmers can report damage on a 14447 helpline, and weather is expected to improve from Saturday afternoon.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Friday asked district magistrates to send district-wise reports on crop damage as the remnants of Cyclone Akvan brought a day of steady, heavy rain to Kolkata and south Bengal. Farmers can report losses on a helpline, 14447, and the agriculture department will carry out a field survey once the weather clears, according to reports.

Nadia recorded the state's heaviest rain, 91.8 mm, and Kolkata between 51.6 mm and 63.1 mm depending on the station, according to reports. Reports differ on the city figure; one put it at 38 mm. Parts of Kolkata and Howrah were waterlogged. No deaths or major damage had been reported in the state by Friday evening, according to reports.

## The review meeting

Mr Adhikari reviewed the situation at Nabanna, the state secretariat, with Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal, Home Secretary Sanghamitra Ghosh and the Director General of Police, and spoke by video conference to the district magistrates and superintendents of police of Purba Medinipur, Howrah, South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Bankura and Jhargram, and to the commissioner of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, according to reports.

He asked for an assessment of how much farmland had been damaged, which crops had been hit and the wider farm situation, and for the reports to be sent quickly so that the government can work out losses, reports said. Officials were told to take precautions against deaths by electrocution, a recurring danger in waterlogged streets, and to act at once on any damage to river embankments. The KMC commissioner was asked to keep the city's drainage and power supply working, according to reports.

The agriculture department's survey will record the affected area in each district, the crops worst hit and farmers' financial losses, and send the figures to the government, according to reports. The government has not said whether compensation will follow. The rain has come during the harvest season for aman paddy, south Bengal's main rice crop.

## The forecast

After crossing the Odisha coast near Gopalpur, Akvan has weakened into a deep depression. It is expected to weaken further into a depression and then a low-pressure area during Saturday, according to reports citing the weather office. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Kolkata kept Kolkata and seven districts on orange alert, with heavy to very heavy rain in isolated places, thunderstorms and gusty winds of 30-50 km/h possible until Saturday afternoon, after which conditions are expected to improve, reports said.

Fishermen have been told not to go to sea. In South 24 Parganas, rivers and the sea were rough, and the administration posted watch at Bakkhali and Gangasagar to stop people from bathing, according to reports. Kolkata Metro cancelled planned Sunday maintenance work because of the rain, one report said.

## What happens next

Dry weather is expected from Tuesday, according to the weather office's earlier forecast. District crop-loss reports are due at Nabanna in the coming days, and the field survey will start once the rain stops.
